note: Per-role parameter distributions mined from professionally designed Surge XT patches (research 141). Target data for patch generation and preset retargeting: the DISTRIBUTION is the finding, not any single value. All times in milliseconds, cutoff in Hz, unison detune in cents (Surge's +/- half-spread convention), resonance on Surge's own 0..1 knob (NOT a biquad Q - not directly comparable to dotbeat's `resonance`, which is Tone.Filter Q).

corpus.source: Surge XT factory + bundled third-party patch banks
corpus.sceneMeasured: the sounding scene: scene_active when scenemode=single, otherwise scene A; dual/split patches also sound scene B, which is not measured

conversions.envelopeTime: seconds = 2 ** raw (Surge ct_envtime, raw range -8..5 => 3.906 ms .. 32 s)
conversions.envelopeTimeFloorNote: raw = -8 is Surge's minimum and its UI DISPLAYS it as '0.00 s'; the digital (default) envelope actually ramps over 2^-8 s = 3.906 ms. 3.906 ms values in this file are that floor.
conversions.unisonDetune: cents = raw * 100 (x12 when extend_range=1); Surge spreads unison voices from -detune to +detune, so this is the +/- HALF spread - total stack width is 2x this number
conversions.envelopeIdentity: env1_* = adsr[0] = amp EG; env2_* = adsr[1] = filter EG
conversions.verification: 500-patch random sample loaded in surgepy and compared against Surge's own getParamDisplay(): cutoff 500/500, resonance 500/500, sustain 500/500, unison detune 419/419, amp-EG decay 482/497, release 473/496, attack 221/494 - every mismatch is the display floor above (Surge prints '0.0 ms' for raw -8).

caveats: Static knob values only: LFO / velocity / macro / mod-matrix routings to these params are NOT resolved, so a patch's sounding cutoff and envelope can differ from the stored value.
cutoffHzKnob is the knob; the sounding cutoff also includes filter keytrack and filter-EG envmod (both reported separately).
Dual- and split-scene patches (15.6% of corpus) sound a second scene that is not measured.
Amp-EG stages that are tempo-synced are excluded from the ms statistics for that stage (1.18% of patches tempo-sync at least one amp-EG stage; 0.84% tempo-sync attack).
Role labels are the patch authors' own directory names, not a listening judgement.
63 of 21,354 stored oscillator unison-voice values were outside Surge's declared 1..16 range (very old streaming revisions) and were clamped exactly as Surge's bound_value() does on load.
